title: SOFF Investment Phase — São Tomé and Príncipe systematic-observations upgrade
description: Investment to strengthen São Tomé and Príncipe's meteorological infrastructure and institutional capacity: upgrade of two automatic weather stations and rehabilitation of one upper-air station, alongside specialised training and strategic management support, targeting compliance with the Global Basic Observing Network (GBON). Approved at the 14th SOFF Steering Committee Meeting, held in Brussels 27–29 May 2026 and co-chaired by WMO and Belgium's Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
recipient_organisation: Democratic Republic of São Tomé and Príncipe

title: Energy Transition, Efficiency and Expansion Project (ETREEP)
description: Grant financing a three-component clean-energy project: 1,000 LED streetlights on São Tomé Island; a new 4MWp solar photovoltaic plant with a 2MWh battery storage system on Príncipe Island; rehabilitation of Príncipe's low-voltage networks and modernisation of the national dispatch centre; and installation of over 40,000 prepaid electricity meters with 2,000 new connections. Targets: billing/collection rates rising from 50% to 80%, non-technical losses falling from 34% to 20%. A cornerstone of São Tomé and Príncipe's National Energy Compact (universal electrification and 50% renewable share by 2030). Roughly 95% of the country's electricity generation currently relies on imported diesel at US$0.30/kWh.
recipient_organisation: Democratic Republic of São Tomé and Príncipe

title: STP Fiscal Sustainability, Energy Access and Digital Connectivity Development Policy Financing
description: Development Policy Financing (budget-support) operation with two pillars: (i) strengthening SOE oversight and fiscal transparency, and (ii) strengthening energy supply and improving digital connectivity. On the digital side, prior actions increase telecoms-sector competition (results indicator: broadband users rising from a 146,000 baseline in Dec/2025 to a 172,000 target by Dec/2028) and set a target of 150,000 people (thousands, 50% female) with digitally verifiable identification by Dec/2028 against a zero baseline. The operation complements the Digital São Tomé and Príncipe Project (P177158, deal wb-stp-001) and the ASCENT regional energy programme, and is coordinated with an IMF Extended Credit Facility programme approved December 2024.
recipient_organisation: Democratic Republic of São Tomé and Príncipe

title: Social Protection, Resilience and Recovery Project — Additional Financing
description: Additional financing to the Social Protection, Resilience and Recovery Project (PPSRR, parent approved 2 May 2022), expanding the number of Vulnerable Family Program beneficiary households by 20% (5,000 to 6,000 households, ~27,600 individuals), extending the project's closing date by one year to 30 June 2028, and continuing investment in the Unique Social Registry (USR, launched 2024, holding data on 8,740 families — ~16% of the national population) and the Ké-Non management information system, an open-source CORE-MIS/openIMIS-based platform adopted in 2024 that is, per the project paper, "for the first time in the country's history... fully owned and operated directly by the government." The AF also continues an electronic cash-transfer payment system built through a partnership with a financial institution, and pilots a new productive-inclusion/self-employment program. The project paper (Report No. PPIAF000203, 12 September 2025) named an expected approval date of 10 September 2025; the financing agreement itself was signed 14 October 2025, per the Bank's own press release, which is taken here as the operative commitment date.
recipient_organisation: Democratic Republic of São Tomé and Príncipe

title: Central African Backbone Program (APL2): Sao Tome and Principe's ACE submarine cable stake
description: Grant financing São Tomé and Príncipe's participation, on an open-access basis, in the Africa Coast to Europe (ACE) optical fibre submarine cable consortium, structured through the special-purpose vehicle STP-Cabo SARL into which government and CST (Companhia São Tomense de Telecomunicações) contributions were made as a long-term shareholder loan. The Implementation Completion and Results Report (Report No. ICR00003141, 17 June 2015) records Board approval on 20 January 2011, effectiveness on 6 July 2011 after a waiver-backed extension, and closing on 31 December 2014, rated Highly Satisfactory. STP paid a US$25m membership fee toward the US$700m ACE consortium investment, of which US$13.1m (52.4%) was financed through this grant, the remainder from Portugal Telecom and CST as private-sector partners. The cable landed in STP in November 2011 and was commercially launched in February 2013. The project also financed technical assistance that led to a second telecommunications licence being awarded to UNITEL International Holdings in 2013, ending CST's monopoly.
recipient_organisation: Democratic Republic of São Tomé and Príncipe
